literal: Military Guards, Part 1
idiomatic: Military Guards, Part 1

literal: The Yellow Emperor combined tally-signs at the Eastern Sea, settled at the ford of Zhuolu, migrated without fixed abode, and used troops as camp and guard.
idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor united tally-signs at the Eastern Sea and settled at Zhuolu; the people moved without fixed homes and took the army as camp and guard.

literal: North of Feihu, east of Wulü, west to the drifting sands—a land of four-sided warfare; even a sage could not escape military guard; such was the terrain.
idiomatic: From north of Feihu to east of Wulü and west to the drifting sands lay a land fought on every side; even a sage could not do without military guard—such was the terrain.

literal: The Liao state held its left at Liaohai and its right at Zhuolu; nowhere was military strength stronger.
idiomatic: The Liao state had Liaohai on the left and Zhuolu on the right; in military power none was stronger.

literal: In Sui times they dwelt along the Heichen River and were divided into ten divisions.
idiomatic: During the Sui they lived by the Heichen River and were split into ten divisions.

literal: Where troops were many there were three thousand; where few, a little over a thousand.
idiomatic: The larger divisions mustered three thousand men, the smaller a little over a thousand.

literal: They followed cold and heat, pursued water and grass, and pastured livestock.
idiomatic: They followed the seasons, moved with water and pasture, and raised herds.

literal: On raids the ten divisions deliberated together; to raise troops and impose service they united tally-signs before moving; on the hunt each division acted on its own.
idiomatic: For invasion the ten divisions met in council; to raise armies and levy service they joined tally-signs before marching, but on the hunt each division went its own way.

literal: By Tang times the Dahe clan had forty-three thousand able troops, divided into eight divisions.
idiomatic: Under the Tang the Dahe clan fielded forty-three thousand fighting men in eight divisions.

literal: The Dahe clan declined; only five divisions remained.
idiomatic: When the Dahe clan waned, only five divisions survived.

literal: Yelü Yali divided the five into eight, established two offices to command them, split three Yelü clans into seven and two Shenmi clans into five—twenty divisions in all.
idiomatic: Yelü Yali split the five divisions into eight, set up two offices to oversee them, broke three Yelü lineages into seven and two Shenmi lineages into five—twenty divisions in all.

literal: They carved wood for tally-contracts and government orders were widely enforced.
idiomatic: Wooden tallies were carved for contracts, and government orders ran through the land.

literal: Xun did not hold the state; the Yaolian clan was raised to replace the Dahe, military strength grew ever stronger—this was the Taizu's sixth-generation ancestor.
idiomatic: When Xun lost the realm the Yaolian clan replaced the Dahe and military power swelled—this was the Taizu's sixth-generation forebear.

literal: When the Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhong he had three hundred thousand troops—mighty indeed.
idiomatic: When the Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhong his host numbered three hundred thousand—a formidable army.

literal: In the tenth year of Yaonian Yelang Khan, the year xinyou, the Taizu received the battle-axe with sole command, broke the Shiwei, Yujue, and Xi states, and captured tents and households beyond counting.
idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yaonian Yelang Khan, the year xinyou, the Taizu was given the battle-axe and sole command; he crushed the Shiwei, Yujue, and Xi and took tents and households past numbering.

literal: In the tenth month he was appointed yilijin of the Dayielie Office, made rewards and punishments clear, repaired armor and weapons, let the people rest, increased the herds, and strove to curb warfare.
idiomatic: In the tenth month he became yilijin of the Dayielie Office: rewards and punishments were made clear, arms were readied, the people were rested, herds were enlarged, and the aim was to still the armies.

literal: In the eleventh year he commanded four hundred thousand troops to attack northern Dai, took nine commanderies and counties, and captured ninety-five thousand persons.
idiomatic: In the eleventh year he led four hundred thousand men against northern Dai, seized nine commanderies and counties, and took ninety-five thousand captives.

literal: In the twelfth year Dezong attacked the Xi and captured seven thousand households.
idiomatic: In the twelfth year Dezong campaigned against the Xi and took seven thousand households.

literal: In the fifteenth year the Yaonian khan died and left orders that the throne pass to the Taizu.
idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Yaonian khan died and commanded that rule pass to the Taizu.

literal: In the fifth year of the Taizu's reign he attacked the western and eastern Xi, pacified them all, and wholly possessed the Xi and Mohe peoples.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of his reign the Taizu attacked western and eastern Xi, subdued them entirely, and held all the Xi and Mohe peoples.

literal: In the sixth spring he personally campaigned against Youzhou; eastern and western banners faced one another for several hundred li.
idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he led a personal campaign on Youzhou; banners east and west stretched for hundreds of li.

literal: Every commandery and county he passed submitted at sight; captives were very many, and he returned in triumph.
idiomatic: Commanderies and counties along the route surrendered at his approach; booty was immense, and he marched home in triumph.

literal: In autumn he personally campaigned against the Beiyin state and captured tens of thousands.
idiomatic: That autumn he personally attacked the Beiyin state and took captives numbering in the tens of thousands.

literal: In the first year of Shence he personally campaigned against the Türks, Tuyuhun, Tangut, lesser tribes, and Shatuo—fifteen thousand six hundred households captured;
idiomatic: In Shence year 1 he personally campaigned against the Türks, Tuyuhun, Tangut, lesser tribes, and Shatuo and took fifteen thousand six hundred households;

literal: he attacked Zhenwu, pressed east on the momentum, attacked the five prefectures of Wei, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, captured beyond counting, and beheaded fourteen thousand seven hundred who would not obey.
idiomatic: he stormed Zhenwu, drove east on the momentum, overran Wei, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, took booty past counting, and slew fourteen thousand seven hundred who refused submission.

literal: He wholly possessed the peoples of northern Dai, the river bend, and the Yin Mountains, and then took the eight armies north of the mountains.
idiomatic: He held all the peoples of northern Dai, the river bend, and the Yin Mountains, then seized the eight armies north of the mountains.

literal: In the fourth year he personally campaigned against the Yuguri state and captured fourteen thousand two hundred persons.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he personally attacked the Yuguri state and took fourteen thousand two hundred captives.

literal: In the fifth year he campaigned against the Tangut and captured two thousand six hundred persons.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he campaigned against the Tangut and took two thousand six hundred captives.

literal: He attacked the Tiande Army, took twelve stockades, and moved the people away.
idiomatic: He assailed the Tiande Army, carried twelve stockades, and relocated the inhabitants.

literal: In the sixth year he went out through Juyong Pass, divided troops to plunder Tan, Shun, and other prefectures, Anyuan Army, Sanhe, Liangxiang, Wangdu, Lu, Mancheng, Suicheng, and other counties, moved captives inland; the crown prince overran Dingzhou and took very many captives.
idiomatic: In the sixth year he issued through Juyong Pass, sent columns to raid Tan, Shun, and other prefectures and Anyuan Army, Sanhe, Liangxiang, Wangdu, Lu, Mancheng, Suicheng, and other counties, moved captives inland, while the crown prince overran Dingzhou with great booty.

literal: In the first year of Tianzan, because households had grown numerous and control was loose, northern Da Nongwu was split into two divisions and two military commissioners were set to command them.
idiomatic: In Tianzan year 1, as households multiplied and oversight grew thin, northern Da Nongwu was divided in two and two commissioners were appointed to command them.

literal: In the third year he campaigned west against the Tangut and other states; captives were beyond counting.
idiomatic: In the third year he marched west against the Tangut and other states and took captives past numbering.

literal: In the fourth year he again personally campaigned against Bohai.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he again led a personal campaign against Bohai.

literal: In the first year of Tianxian he destroyed the Bohai state—territory five thousand li, troops several hundred thousand, five capitals, fifteen prefectures, sixty-two prefectures—and wholly possessed their peoples; the Khitan grew greater still.
idiomatic: In Tianxian year 1 he destroyed Bohai—five thousand li of territory, armies in the hundreds of thousands, five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts—and held all their people; Khitan power swelled further.

literal: At the beginning of Huitong the Taizong destroyed Tang and established Jin; Jin offered the sixteen prefectures of Yan and Dai—the people numerous and troops strong, none could withstand them.
idiomatic: At the opening of Huitong the Taizong ended Tang and raised Jin; Jin surrendered Yan and Dai's sixteen prefectures—populous lands and strong armies that none could resist.

literal: ○ Military System
idiomatic: ○ Military System

literal: Liao military regulations: all commoners from fifteen up to fifty were entered on military registers.
idiomatic: Under Liao military law every man from fifteen to fifty was registered for service.

literal: For each regular soldier one foraging-camp retainer and one camp-guard retainer; three horses per man.
idiomatic: Each regular soldier had three horses plus one foraging-camp retainer and one camp-guard retainer.

literal: Nine iron armor pieces per man, horse saddle and bridle, horse armor of leather and iron according to strength;
idiomatic: Each man bore nine pieces of iron armor; saddle, bridle, and horse armor of leather and iron were allotted by strength;

literal: four bows, four hundred arrows, long and short spears, mattocks and hooked tools, axes and halberds, small flags, hammer-awls, fire-stone knives, horse cups—each short one peck.
idiomatic: four bows, four hundred arrows, long and short spears, mattocks and hooked tools, axes and halberds, small flags, hammer-awls, fire-stone knives, and horse cups—each man one peck short in grain.

literal: One small pouch and one felt umbrella each, two hundred feet of tether rope—all self-provided.
idiomatic: Each also carried one small pouch and one felt umbrella and two hundred feet of tether rope, all at his own cost.

literal: Men and horses were not issued grain or fodder; daily they sent foraging cavalry in four directions to raid and supply them.
idiomatic: Neither men nor horses received rations; each day foraging cavalry rode out in four directions to plunder for supplies.

literal: Gold fish tallies were cast to mobilize armies and horses.
idiomatic: They cast gold fish tallies to dispatch armies and horses.

literal: Those who seized horses and bore orders had two hundred silver plaques.
idiomatic: Horse-catchers and order-bearers held two hundred silver plaques.

literal: Where the army encamped there were distant-scout barricade horse scouts to listen at night for the sound of men and horses.
idiomatic: At every camp distant-scout barricade horse scouts listened through the night for the sound of men and horses.

literal: Whenever troops were raised the emperor led Khitan and Han civil and military officials, sacrificed with blue ox and white horse to Heaven and Earth and the sun god—only not bowing to the moon—and separately ordered close ministers to announce to the tombs from the Taizu down and to the god of Mount Muye, then decreed levies from every circuit.
idiomatic: When armies were raised the emperor led Khitan and Han officials, offered blue ox and white horse to Heaven, Earth, and the sun—never the moon—and sent close ministers to report to the tombs from the Taizu onward and to Mount Muye's god before decreeing levies on every circuit.

literal: Only the southern king, northern king, Xi king, Eastern Capital Bohai troops, and Yanjing commander-in-chief's troops—though they received the decree—dared not march until they had reported.
idiomatic: Even the southern king, northern king, Xi king, Eastern Capital Bohai forces, and Yanjing commander's troops, though they received the decree, would not march until they had reported to the throne.

literal: The court dispatched a great general bearing the gold fish tally; only when tallies matched did they move.
idiomatic: The court sent a great general with the gold fish tally; only when the tallies joined did the columns march.

literal: At first word of the decree they gathered household men, weighed household strength, checked registers, and mustered the host to wait.
idiomatic: On first hearing the decree they mustered household men, weighed each household's capacity, reconciled registers, and assembled the host to wait.

literal: From commanders of ten upward they mustered troops and gear in sequence.
idiomatic: From leaders of ten men upward they mustered troops and weapons in due order.

literal: When the tally arrived the original bureau led the troops itself; envoys might not take command.
idiomatic: When the tally arrived the home bureau itself led the troops; the envoy might not take them over.

literal: Only after jointly counting the troops again did they report upward.
idiomatic: Only after a second joint muster of troops and gear did they report upward.

literal: According to the size of the force they again appointed an envoy as army commander to supervise jointly with the home bureau.
idiomatic: They gauged the host's size and again named an envoy as army commander to supervise jointly with the home bureau.

literal: They also requested the five-direction banners and drums; then the emperor personally inspected officers.
idiomatic: They also called for the five-direction banners and drums; only then did the emperor personally review the officers.

literal: Meritorious kin and great ministers were again chosen as camp army commander, deputy commander, and overseer, one each.
idiomatic: Meritorious kin and great ministers were chosen as camp army commander, deputy commander, and overseer, one of each.

literal: From every army the finest thirty thousand were chosen as the imperial guard corps; three thousand bold men as vanguard; groups of a hundred or more of the fiercest as distant-scout barricade horse corps—each with its own officers.
idiomatic: From all armies thirty thousand elite troops formed the imperial guard; three thousand daring men the vanguard; bands of a hundred or more of the boldest the distant-scout barricade horse corps—each with its officers.

literal: Again in each army unit.
idiomatic: Again, within each army unit:

literal: According to numbers, five or ten men were drawn from each unit, formed into a squad with its own leader, to requisition troops and relay official business.
idiomatic: By strength, five or ten men were taken from each unit, formed into a squad under its own leader, to levy troops and carry urgent dispatches.

literal: For southern campaigns troops were mustered mostly a thousand li north of Youzhou at Mandarin-Duck Marsh.
idiomatic: Southern campaigns were mustered chiefly at Mandarin-Duck Marsh, a thousand li north of Youzhou.

literal: On the march they took the routes of Juyong Pass, Caowang Vale, White Horse Ford, Gubei Pass, Anda Horse Ford, Songting Pass, Yuguan, and the rest.
idiomatic: On the march they used Juyong Pass, Caowang Vale, White Horse Ford, Gubei Pass, Anda Horse Ford, Songting Pass, Yuguan, and the like.

literal: As they neared Pingzhou and Youzhou territory envoys were again sent on separate roads to hurry them on—they might not linger long, lest they trample the grain.
idiomatic: Near Pingzhou and Youzhou they sent envoys on separate roads to hurry the columns—they could not linger, lest they tread the crops.

literal: Troops might not issue after the ninth month; return might not pass the twelfth month.
idiomatic: Armies might not march out after the ninth month nor return after the twelfth.

literal: On the road they might not meet monks, nuns, or persons in mourning dress.
idiomatic: On the march they might not encounter monks, nuns, or mourners in funeral dress.

literal: When the emperor campaigned in person one close prince was left at Youzhou to act for military and state affairs.
idiomatic: When the emperor led the campaign himself one imperial prince remained at Youzhou with authority over army and state.

literal: Once within the southern border they divided into three routes—Guangxin Army, Xiongzhou, and Bazhou each one.
idiomatic: South of the border they split into three columns—Guangxin Army, Xiongzhou, and Bazhou each had one.

literal: The imperial carriage must take the middle road; the army commander and guard corps all followed.
idiomatic: The imperial carriage always took the center; the army commander and guard corps followed it.

literal: Troops on each route attacked county seats and towns as soon as they met them.
idiomatic: Each column attacked every county seat and market town it met.

literal: Against great prefectural armies they first gauged strength and feasible order of attack before advancing.
idiomatic: Before a great prefectural army they first judged its strength and the sequence in which it could be taken.

literal: Along the way they leveled and burned gardens, orchards, and mulberry and catalpa groves.
idiomatic: Along the route they cut down and burned gardens, orchards, and mulberry and catalpa plantings.

literal: At the Song Northern Capital all three armies met to deliberate the assault.
idiomatic: At the Song Northern Capital the three hosts united to plan the assault.

literal: On retreat it was the same.
idiomatic: On the withdrawal it was the same.

literal: Before, behind, left, and right of the three armies were vanguards.
idiomatic: Vanguards rode before, behind, left, and right of the three armies.

literal: Distant-scout barricade horse scouts, a dozen or so each, lay twenty-odd li before and behind the vanguard, in full armor; at night they marched ten or five li and halted briefly, dismounted and listened sideways for the sound of men and horses.
idiomatic: Barricade horse scouts in bands of a dozen lay twenty-odd li ahead and behind the vanguard in full armor; at night they rode ten or five li, halted briefly, dismounted, and listened for men or horses.

literal: If there were any, they seized them.
idiomatic: Anyone detected was seized.

literal: If strength could not match the enemy, they flew word to the vanguard and attacked together.
idiomatic: If they could not overcome the foe they raced word to the vanguard and struck together.

literal: If there was a great army they ran to report the commander.
idiomatic: If a great host appeared they galloped to warn the commander.

literal: The enemy's true strength and movements were always known.
idiomatic: The enemy's real strength and every movement were always known.

literal: When the army passed a prefectural city on the main road that was stoutly defended and could not be taken, they led the troops past it.
idiomatic: If a prefectural city on the main road was too strong to storm, they led the host past it.

literal: Fearing the enemy would sally to intercept, they surrounded it, shot arrows, and shouted as if attacking.
idiomatic: Lest the garrison sally to block them, they ringed the walls, shot, and shouted as though attacking.

literal: The enemy shut the gates and held firm; the road ahead was clear, the army advanced, and detachments cut communications so every prefectural city stood isolated without aid.
idiomatic: The foe barred the gates; the road ahead lay open; the host pressed on while detachments severed links so every city stood alone without relief.

literal: At every large or small prefectural city by night—fearing troops would sally or neighboring prefectures would combine forces—at the first watch a hundred horsemen went a hundred-odd paces from each gate in armor with weapons, standing by their mounts.
idiomatic: At night, at every city great or small, lest the garrison sally or neighboring forces unite, at the first watch a hundred horsemen in armor with weapons waited a hundred paces from each gate beside their mounts.

literal: If troops came out and strength could not prevail, they galloped back to gather the host and fight.
idiomatic: If the enemy sallied and they could not prevail, they raced back to muster the host and give battle.

literal: Official highways, bypaths, mountain roads, and river crossings were all patrolled by night.
idiomatic: Main roads, side paths, mountain tracks, and river fords were patrolled through the night.

literal: Foraging-camp retainers each wore armor and bore arms, wheeling into squads; they first cut orchards, then drove off the old and young, hauled earth and timber to fill moats and ditches, and at assault must climb first—stones, bolts, and beams fell only on the old and young.
idiomatic: Foraging-camp retainers wore armor, formed rotating squads, felled orchards first, then drove off the aged and children and hauled earth and timber to fill ditches; at the assault they climbed first while missiles fell mainly on the old and young.

literal: From home prefectures and counties ten thousand Han militia were also raised to march with the army, dedicated to felling gardens and filling roads.
idiomatic: From the realm's prefectures and counties ten thousand Han militia marched with the host to fell gardens and fill roads.

literal: Imperial camps and all stockades used only mulberry, catalpa, pear, and chestnut.
idiomatic: Imperial camps and every stockade used only mulberry, catalpa, pear, and chestnut.

literal: On withdrawal they set fire and burned them.
idiomatic: On withdrawal they burned them all.

literal: Once the enemy had formed battle lines they gauged the formation's size, the mountains and rivers, roads in and out, rescue shortcuts, and where supplies came from—each had its counter.
idiomatic: When the enemy formed ranks they measured the array, terrain, roads, relief paths, and supply lines—each had its countermeasure.

literal: Then on four sides of the formation cavalry were ranged in squads of five to seven hundred; ten squads made a file, ten files a front.
idiomatic: Then on all four sides of the enemy line cavalry stood in squads of five to seven hundred; ten squads a file, ten files a front.

literal: Each had its commander.
idiomatic: Each front had its commander.

literal: The foremost squad galloped with great shouting and charged the enemy line.
idiomatic: The leading squad galloped shouting and smashed into the enemy line.

literal: If they prevailed, all squads advanced together.
idiomatic: On success every squad charged together.

literal: If they did not prevail they withdrew; the second squad followed.
idiomatic: If they failed they drew off and the second squad took their place.

literal: Those who withdrew rested horses, drank water, and fed fodder.
idiomatic: The withdrawn men rested their horses, watered them, and fed grain.

literal: Every file did the same.
idiomatic: Every file did likewise.

literal: They advanced again in rotation; if the enemy line did not move they did not press hard either.
idiomatic: They rotated forward in waves; if the enemy line held firm they did not press the fight.

literal: After two or three days, when the foe was weary, foraging-camp retainers were ordered to fit double brooms on their horses and ride with the wind, raising dust across the enemy line back and forth.
idiomatic: After two or three days, when the foe was spent, foraging retainers fixed double brooms to their horses and rode with the wind, whipping dust across the enemy ranks back and forth.

literal: Midst hunger and exhaustion they could not see one another and victory could be taken.
idiomatic: Hungry and worn, the enemy could scarcely see one another—and victory could be won.

literal: If the southern wing won and the northern wing lost, the commander in the center could not know; they used the realm's mountains and rivers as signals, calling by name to rescue one another.
idiomatic: If the southern wing won while the northern wing lost, the commander at the center might not know; they called by the names of the homeland's mountains and rivers to signal and rescue one another.

literal: If the emperor did not campaign in person, a great minister commanding no fewer than a hundred fifty thousand followed the three routes there and back, mustering at the Northern Capital—out in the ninth month, back in the twelfth—the sequence of actions was the same.
idiomatic: If the emperor stayed home, a great minister led no fewer than a hundred fifty thousand on the three routes, mustering at the Northern Capital—out in the ninth month, back in the twelfth—with the same sequence of actions.
